away.headline: Bears estimated injury report: Elijah Hicks ruled out, Kyler Gordon still no practice
away.blurb: The Chicago Bears are hoping to be as close to full strength as possible against the Detroit Lions on Thanksgiving Day, but there are still some things to figure out. Gordon has missed six games this season due to injuries, with five of them being soft-tissue lower-leg injuries, while also missing Chicago's Week 11 win over the New Orleans Saints with a shoulder injury. With two straight days of "DNP" statuses, it doesn't look good for him to play in one of the biggest games of the season. Tuesday Status: DNP (Ruled out of Lions game via Bears HC Ben Johnson) A new surprise to the injury report was announced before the second one came out, as Johnson told reporters that Hicks was in concussion protocol and was ruled out for the Lions contest. NFL rules state that a player must be in concussion protocol for at least five days before being cleared, so that will not be enough time for the Bears to get Hicks back. Here is the good news that the Bears needed: Benedet is listed as a full participant. He was listed as "DNP" on the first injury report after hurting his quad in the Saints game. Benedet was only out for a short time before coming back into the game fairly quickly. Ozzy Trapilo is his backup if the Bears need Benedet to sit out, but Chicago would rather not have Trapilo play yet. This is a good sign that the Bears' offensive line should be intact for the Lions game. Phillips and Lewis did well filling in at slot corner in the Saints game, so the Bears should still get some good production there, even with Gordon missing the game. It will hurt the Bears' depth at safety and on special teams, with Hicks as a key player. Chicago should be able to hold their own with Dillon Thieneman and Lewis starting at safety. The Bears were assigned Isaac Yiadom from waivers on Tuesday, so he could end up taking Hicks's spot on the 53-man roster. That's two straight days Roschon Johnson hasn't been listed as a participant after leaving the Saints game early with an ankle injury. home.headline: Detroit Lions rule CB out, list two starters questionable vs. Bears
home.blurb: Lions head coach Dan Campbell announced on Tuesday that rookie defensive lineman Skyler Gill-Howard had suffered a season-ending knee injury . Naturally, Gill-Howard was listed out on the game status report. Cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. was also ruled out with a shoulder injury. Rakestraw has played in seven games this season, starting one. The 5-foot-11, 192-pound corner has registered 11 tackles, two pass breakups and one forced fumble this season. Starting safety Chuck Clark (hamstring) and EDGE DJ Wonnum (back) were both listed as questionable. Starting cornerback D.J. Reed (hip) is cleared and ready to make his return after missing each of the Lions' past three games against the Dolphins , Patriots , and Buccaneers . Tight end Sam LaPorta (ankle) and cornerback Khalil Dorsey (wrist) also both came off the injury report, and are cleared to play against the Bears . Rakestraw, a 2024 second-round pick out of Missouri, entered the 2026 NFL season having played in just eight NFL games as he's battled hamstring and shoulder injuries throughout his career. away.headline: CeeDee Lamb's bold claim ahead of Thanksgiving gives Eagles' star cornerback something to prove against Cowboys
away.blurb: The last time the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys met on Thanksgiving, Mark Sanchez dismantled them 33-10 and Philly took over the NFC East lead. That game is still one of my fondest holiday memories. Now the Eagles get another crack at the Cowboys on Thursday, and the injury news is big. Running back Saquon Barkley was a full participant at practice with his neck stinger, and cornerback Quinyon Mitchell was limited. Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb also just handed Mitchell some fresh bulletin board material. That season eventually fell apart. Sanchez lost three straight, and Nick Foles was out with a broken collarbone. But the Birds have been historically good on Thanksgiving. I have them at 6-1. Maybe Joe Milton has a little revenge game in him this time around. That's why Barkley against the Cowboys' defensive line is key No. 1. Barkley has scored a touchdown in four straight games he's played in, and the offensive line has gotten better. Philly still can't figure out its offense for four full quarters. But the Cowboys rank 32nd in yards allowed per play and 32nd in rushing defense, giving up 151.5 rushing yards per game. They changed play-callers to Mike Pettine, and it doesn't matter. That defense has no talent. Credit to Prescott, he plays well against the Birds. I still think he's a regular season merchant, just a really good one. The Eagles have to force the ball out of his hands under pressure and stop giving up yards after the catch. Will he even throw at Mitchell? Maybe Dallas goes after Tariq Woolen with Pickens all day. Woolen wasn't happy about being benched, and Cooper DeJean could factor in too. home.headline: CeeDee Lamb's bold claim ahead of Thanksgiving gives Eagles' star cornerback something to prove against Cowboys
home.blurb: The last time the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys met on Thanksgiving, Mark Sanchez dismantled them 33-10 and Philly took over the NFC East lead. That game is still one of my fondest holiday memories. Now the Eagles get another crack at the Cowboys on Thursday, and the injury news is big. Running back Saquon Barkley was a full participant at practice with his neck stinger, and cornerback Quinyon Mitchell was limited. Cowboys wide receiver CeeDee Lamb also just handed Mitchell some fresh bulletin board material. That season eventually fell apart. Sanchez lost three straight, and Nick Foles was out with a broken collarbone. But the Birds have been historically good on Thanksgiving. I have them at 6-1. Maybe Joe Milton has a little revenge game in him this time around. That's why Barkley against the Cowboys' defensive line is key No. 1. Barkley has scored a touchdown in four straight games he's played in, and the offensive line has gotten better. Philly still can't figure out its offense for four full quarters. But the Cowboys rank 32nd in yards allowed per play and 32nd in rushing defense, giving up 151.5 rushing yards per game. They changed play-callers to Mike Pettine, and it doesn't matter. That defense has no talent. Credit to Prescott, he plays well against the Birds. I still think he's a regular season merchant, just a really good one. The Eagles have to force the ball out of his hands under pressure and stop giving up yards after the catch. Will he even throw at Mitchell? Maybe Dallas goes after Tariq Woolen with Pickens all day. Woolen wasn't happy about being benched, and Cooper DeJean could factor in too. away.headline: Bills list Benford, Kincaid, 3 others questionable vs. Chiefs
away.blurb: ORCHARD PARK, N.Y. — Christian Benford didn’t practice Monday. By Tuesday he was a limited participant in a walk-through, and that’s about all the Buffalo Bills had to go on before Wednesday’s final injury report. Benford is questionable for Thursday night’s game against the Kansas City Chiefs. Four other players have the same designation: tight end Dalton Kincaid (thumb/ankle), defensive tackle T.J. Sanders (shoulder), guard O’Cyrus Torrence (ankle) and linebacker Dorian Williams (calf). Kincaid, Sanders, Torrence and Williams were limited all week. Every one of them except Torrence sat out Sunday’s 26-9 win over Miami. Kansas City has its own problems. Kenneth Walker III will miss his third straight game with a groin injury, and right tackle Jaylon Moore and defensive tackle Omar Norman-Lott are also out. Tight end Noah Gray and defensive lineman Peter Woods are questionable. Benford has been Buffalo’s most reliable outside corner all season. If Benford can’t play, that’ll mean second-year cornerback Maxwell Hairston—benched earlier this season for rookie Davison Igbinosun—will start in his place. Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard was complimentary of Hairston after his performance last week against the Miami Dolphins. “I thought he played well,” Leonhard said. “I thought he challenged; he played with consistency. Again, not many big splash plays. He gets the PBU (pass breakup), but I thought he was very consistent. Probably the most consistent he’s been all season.” Kincaid’s situation is just as important on the other side of the ball. He went for over 100 yards receiving and a touchdown against the Chiefs last season. Torrence played through an ankle injury last week, and he’ll be another name to watch. Austin Corbett is probably first up off the bench, but he’s only played left guard this season for the Bills. Torrence has never missed a start in his 61-game NFL career. The Bills are 3-point favorites. ©2026 Advance Local Media LLC. Visit syracuse.com. Distributed by Tribune Content Agency, LLC.

Sanders (shoulder), guard O’Cyrus Torrence (ankle) and linebacker Dorian Williams (calf). Kincaid, Sanders, Torrence and Williams were limited all week. Every one of them except Torrence sat out Sunday’s 26-9 win over Miami. Kansas City has its own problems. Kenneth Walker III will miss his third straight game with a groin injury, and right tackle Jaylon Moore and defensive tackle Omar Norman-Lott are also out. Tight end Noah Gray and defensive lineman Peter Woods are questionable. Benford has been Buffalo’s most reliable outside corner all season. If Benford can’t play, that’ll mean second-year cornerback Maxwell Hairston—benched earlier this season for rookie Davison Igbinosun—will start in his place. Bills defensive coordinator Jim Leonhard was complimentary of Hairston after his performance last week against the Miami Dolphins. “I thought he played well,” Leonhard said. “I thought he challenged; he played with consistency. Again, not many big splash plays. He gets the PBU (pass breakup), but I thought he was very consistent. Probably the most consistent he’s been all season.” Kincaid’s situation is just as important on the other side of the ball. He went for over 100 yards receiving and a touchdown against the Chiefs last season. Torrence played through an ankle injury last week, and he’ll be another name to watch. Austin Corbett is probably first up off the bench, but he’s only played left guard this season for the Bills. Torrence has never missed a start in his 61-game NFL career.
